Created attachment 2944
Sample package illustrating the bug

The attached package contains two vignettes.  The first one creates a function called `mean` which prints a message; the second calls `mean(1:5)`, presumably expecting to execute `base::mean`, but runs the function from the first vignette instead.

This issue originated on StackOverflow and was discussed in R-devel in https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-devel/2021-October/081197.html .

The problem is that `R CMD build` starts a clean new session and runs `tools::buildVignettes()` there, but that function runs all the vignettes in the same session.  The suggested fix is for `buildVignettes` to start a new session for each vignette to guarantee isolation between them.

Created attachment 3826
Reuse the ser_elibs argument for tools::buildVignettes()

The minimal option: make `R CMD build` use the same `ser_elibs` argument that `R CMD check` already uses by default. Likely needs further fixing so that `buildVignettes` tangles the vignettes into `*.R` files even when running separate processes per vignette.

Created attachment 3827
Add a 'separate' argument to buildVignettes

A refactoring of `tools::buildVignettes` and places were `R CMD build` and `R CMD check` call it. Instead of passing a path to a temporary file containing the environment, rely on the child processes to inherit it from the parent (both `R CMD build` and `R CMD check` pass these environment variables when launching a process to run `buildVignettes()`).

This can also be rewritten to use `deparse1()` to avoid both quoting hell and temporary files.

The `elibs` argument could also be added back if setting the environment variables twice, both in the parent running `buildVignettes` and the children running `tools:::.buildOneVignette`, is necessary.
